title: Cutover safety checklist, rollback matrix, and mini calendar (Sep 2025) - WIP
summary: Working draft: concise pre-cutover safety checklist, a simple rollback decision matrix, and an hour-by-hour mini calendar for the cutover window. Purpose is to give on-call and release leads a fast reference during the weekend cutover.
body:
Purpose:
This is an operational working doc to be used during the next platform cutover (target: 2025-09-20). It collects the minimal safety checks, decision triggers for rollback, and a compact hour-by-hour calendar for the engineering, SRE, and product on-call teams.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated control-plane changes only (no DB schema migration requiring backfill).
- Targeted traffic switch uses feature flags + smart routing (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Canary window will be controlled via RL feature-flag service and circuit-breaker guardrails.
- Expected outage tolerance: <5 minutes for any single region; full rollback path must restore last stable build within 15 minutes.

Pre-cutover safety checklist (must be green before starting):
- Release artifacts verified:
  - Build: CI-green for release branch, all integration tests passed (link: GitHub PR in linked_artifacts).
  - Image availability: container registry has tagged images for all services.
  - Migration: zero DB schema migrations in this release. If migrations exist, schedule separate window.
- Observability sanity:
  - Dashboards bookmarked for latency, error rate, request rate, and internal queue depth.
  - Synthetic tests healthy for 24h for primary regions.
  - Tracing available and sampling enabled for canary traffic.
- Capacity and throttles:
  - Autoscaling policies validated in staging and a smoke test ramp performed last 48h.
  - Token bucket and concurrency limits checked for new endpoints.
- Rollback and fallback ready:
  - Previous stable image tag documented in release notes draft section below.
  - Feature-flag rollback path pre-configured and tested (toggle + immediate traffic re-route).
  - Fallback region list and DNS TTLs known (expected DNS propagation < 60s where supported).
- Communication and pager plan:
  - Slack channel #rel-cutover-2025 created and all participants invited.
  - On-call list: primary release lead, SRE lead, DB SME (if needed), infra eng, and product owner.
  - Pager escalation policy verified and audible pager numbers confirmed.
- External dependencies:
  - Cloud provider maintenance windows checked; no conflicts.
  - Any third-party services with IP allowlists updated.

Cutover mini calendar (hour-by-hour; times in UTC):
- T-02:00: Final signoff call (30m) - release lead + SRE + product - verify green on checklist items, confirm rollback assets.
- T-01:00: Pre-cutover smoke: run synthetic smoke suite against canary cluster (15m).
- T-00:30: Warn stakeholders: post a message to #rel-cutover-2025 with expected start, brief rollback criteria, and contact list.
- T-00:00: Start canary rollout (5% traffic) + open monitoring window. Ops: watch latency and error-rate dashboards.
- T+00:15: If canary healthy -> increase to 25%. If not -> evaluate triggers (see rollback matrix).
- T+00:45: 25% hold window (30m) -> validate SLA and infra metrics, run subset of production load tests.
- T+01:15: If green -> 50% (10m ramp).
- T+01:45: 50% hold (30m).
- T+02:15: Final ramp to 100% (gradual ramp over 10m).
- T+02:30: Post-cutover stabilization (1h) - daily ETL/async jobs monitored, background queues observed.
- T+03:30: Post-release sync call (15m) - release lead summarizes outcome, decide if further rollouts (other regions) proceed.

Decision / rollback matrix (quick reference):
- Metrics being watched (primary):
  - 5xx error rate (api): threshold = >0.5% sustained for 5m.
  - p95 latency increase: threshold = >2x from baseline sustained for 10m.
  - Internal queue depth/backpressure: threshold = sustained increase of >30% and growing for 10m.
  - Customer-impacting alerts: any SLA breach triggered in top-level alerting rule.

- Actions by severity:
  - Severity A (Immediate rollback):
    - Trigger: 5xx >1% for 3m OR p95 >3x baseline for 3m OR major queue blocking causing request backpressure.
    - Action: Toggle feature-flag to route traffic to last-stable tag -> follow rollback checklist (see below).
    - Expected RTO: restore baseline traffic within 10 minutes.
  - Severity B (Pause + investigate):
    - Trigger: 0.5% < 5xx <= 1% OR p95 >2x but <3x baseline, or transient partial degradations affecting <20% of routes.
    - Action: Pause ramp, roll back last step (e.g., move from 25% back to 5%), collect traces, notify product and SRE.
    - Expected RTO: 15-30 minutes to stabilize or escalate to Severity A.
  - Severity C (Degraded but acceptable):
    - Trigger: minor increases in latency (<2x p95) or low-level error noise not tied to deploy.
    - Action: Continue with caution, increase monitoring, schedule postmortem investigation if persistent.

Rollback quick checklist (ordered):
1) Announce rollback in #rel-cutover-2025 with reason and immediate expected impact.
2) Toggle feature flag to previous state (document exact flag and API call).
3) Verify traffic shift observed in traffic graphs and that % of errors drops.
4) Promote last-stable images to active tag if flag toggle insufficient.
5) If traffic still shows systemic failure, perform DNS failover to fallback region (pre-approved list).
6) Open outage incident page and assign owner for postmortem.

Runbook snippets (commands and quick pointers):
- Feature flag rollback (example): curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/toggle -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"flag":"release-new-routing","state":"off"}'
- Promote stable image (example): kubectl set image deployment/api api=registry.redwood:stable-20250823 -n prod
- Emergency eviction of canary pods: kubectl delete pod -l rollouts=canary -n prod --grace-period=0 --force

Release notes (draft - to be trimmed for customer-facing):
- Summary: This release completes the routing refactor that enables smart multi-region failover and per-customer routing policies.
- Notable changes:
  - New routing service (routing-v2) behind the routing feature flag; incremental rollouts planned.
  - Observability: higher-fidelity tracing for inter-service calls, added latency histograms on API gateway.
  - Performance: reduced median token latency for hosted-api by ~10% in internal benchmarks.
- Breaking / migration notes: No customer-facing schema changes. Some internal metrics names changed (dashboards updated).
- Rollout plan: canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback criteria as described above.
- Known issues: small number of 403s observed in staging when alternate auth header present (workaround: clear stale auth proxies).

Post-release monitoring and follow-ups (first 48h):
- 0-6h: hourly checks and Slack updates from release lead.
- 6-24h: every 2h checks, SRE lead to review error budget consumption.
- 24-48h: daily sync for final sign-off and to decide regional rollouts.
- Postmortem: if any rollback occurred or any Severity B incident, kickoff 72h postmortem and include action items assigned in ticket REL-2026.

Open questions / TODOs (items to resolve before finalizing playbook):
- Confirm DNS failover TTLs for eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 (action: infra team).
- Verify fallback region capacity for 100% traffic (action: capacity planning spreadsheet).
- Finalize list of external vendors to notify in the event of cross-region failover.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider automating the decision tree into a small lambda that can suggest rollback vs pause (low priority).
- Might add quick mobile alert (SMS) for release lead if Severity A triggers outside office hours.

Appendix: quick contacts
- Release lead: Marcus Li (pager x232)
- SRE lead: Priya Nair (pager x109)
- Infra: Ethan Park
- Product owner: Rosa Martinez
- Paging escalation doc: Confluence link in linked_artifacts

End of working draft. This doc will be consolidated into the official playbook after rehearsal and signoff.
